findings.issue: .env pattern only ignores the exact file '.env'; does not cover .env.local, .env.production, .env.development, .env.test. If a developer creates .env.production with production secrets and runs git add, they will be committed.
findings.regressions_risked: Future dotenv usage (no current usage found) could result in production credentials being committed. Attack vector: CWE-312 / CWE-200.
findings.durable_check: git ls-files | grep -E '\.env\.' — should return empty; run after any new .env.* file creation
findings.claim: .env pattern is narrower than standard defensive gitignore practice

evidence.rationale: git check-ignore returns nothing if file is not ignored; 'NOT IGNORED' if unignored
